when i am have troubling sleeping, the two things that absolutely always help are:

1) take long, measured inhales and exhales.. the slower and longer the better! it stimulates your parasympathetic nervous system, whose entire job is to decrease stress, anxiety, and heart rate to put you in a more relaxed state.

2) visualize how things and places look!!! if you catch yourself slipping into thinking things *about* how they look, it's okay, but catch yourself and return to just seeing them and "looking" at them.. when you do this, it engages a brain circuit called the septohippocampal system which is actually two structures communicating back and forth. when you engage in visualization like this, it promotes brain waves in the 4-8 Hz range (called theta waves), which will take away the sensation of racing thoughts by slowing the speed at which the brain processes.

enjoy your rest!!!!  💚💚

$SPY weekly momentum has been in bearish territory since July, and we’ve barely been able to make new highs. This is the third time in less than two years that weekly momentum has been bearish while $SPY was pushing to new highs.

1. Q4 2024 - Q1 2025 — Weekly momentum entered bearish territory in the final, full trading week of 2024 and was never able to reclaim bullish momentum. $SPY rallied to marginal, new highs, peaking 8 weeks later, before selling -21.43% over the following 8 weeks.

2. Q4 2025 - Q1 2026 — Weekly momentum entered bearish territory at the November 2025 low and was never able to reclaim bullish momentum. $SPY rallied to marginal, new highs, peaking 10 weeks later, before selling -9.82% over the following 10 weeks.

3. Q3 2026 - Q4 2026 — Weekly momentum entered bearish territory in mid-July and hasn’t yet been able to reclaim bullish momentum. $SPY was able to rally to a marginal, new high in August before selling -3.82% over the following 6 weeks. Weekly momentum is still in bearish territory, and $SPY just rallied to yet another marginal, new high. I cannot be bullish until weekly momentum flips back to bullish.

Rallies with bearish momentum are almost always met with retracements. There’s an incredibly strong probability that we get a solid retracement in the coming days / weeks based on what I’m seeing.

The hardest lessons I’ve learned in 7 years of trading (bookmark this)

Drawdown is a normal part of the game. This game is about lasting not new highs on the account every day. 

The worst time to trade 0dte is when the $VIX is sub 15. You’re more likely to grind sideways than get big trends on $SPY $QQQ. 

Daily max loss and weekly loss rules are mandatory to prevent torching accounts. Knowing when your mind isn’t in the right place is a skill not a weakness. 

Breaks are wonderful I take several weeks off during my worst performing periods from the last 7 years of trading data. 

Trading can be frustrating taking 10 losing trades in a row is normal as per probability. You may feel the market is against you but it’s not. It’s just math. 

To make 10k a day you need a solid 20k red day mega tilt day. To make $x,xxx you need to lose it first. Humans learn from mistakes. No body ever learned from luck. 

The market runs in cycles of hot and cold. If the market is cold reducing size and frequency is how you have the MENTAL capital to push big size during hot cycles. 

Stocks without news are more likely to chop you up. Names with news remain at the top my watchlist everyday. 

A setup gets 2 attempts. The third try is almost always a trap. So make sure you playbook the trap setups to take advantage. 

Multi time frame analysis is mandatory. The time frames all dance with each other so you must learn to tango so you don’t trip over yourself. 

You need a toolbox. Swing trading and day trading. If you tell people you only stick to one your equity curve will likely remain flat for extended periods of times. This is okay but just be aware of the pros and cons of each. 

Lastly, trading is really hard. But I’d rather lock in for 2 years then spend my life at a job for 40 years and still have the thought of “what if I gave it my all?”

Small-account traders, this one's for you! 

You don't need a $50K account to learn options trading.

If I were starting with $3K - $5K today, I'd focus on SPY or XSP instead of jumping straight into SPX 0DTE.

Start with 1 - 2 contracts, learn to manage risk, and focus on consistency.

Forget making $1,000 a day. Learn how to protect your capital first.

Your first goal isn't to get rich. It's to survive long enough to become a consistently disciplined trader.

Small accounts can grow. Blown accounts can't.
